newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Man unfazed by sticky commodities H1.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Man unfazed by sticky commodities H1.

text.p: British-based commodities and financial services group ED & F Man said on Thursday it was on course for improved full-year results, despite reporting soft first half profits from some of its agricultural businesses.

Group pretax profits for the six months to September 30 edged back to 27.2 million pounds ($45.7 million) from 32.8 million in the same year-ago period but Man raised its interim dividend by 6.0 percent to 3.4 pence.

Group managing director Harvey McGrath said this dividend rise reflected Man's continued confidence in a satisfactory outcome for the year as a whole, and added "some encouraging (recent) developments in the business have reinforced this".

In particular, he said, the level of commodities business already contracted for the second half confirmed the expectation of a seasonal trend pattern that "typically translates into increased activity in the second half of our financial year".
Last year Man's twelve month pretax profit was 81.1 million pounds, up 4.0 percent year-on-year, and most share analysts have been forecasting a similar increase for 1996/97.

According to Edinburgh Financial Publishing data on Reuters 3000, a recent consensus estimate of six share analysts' forecasts is for pre-tax profit of 84.5 million pounds in the year to next March -- up 4.3 percent.
The same analysts expect a total dividend of 10.7 pence per share, up 5.4 percent on 1995/96.

With the firm increase in interim dividend on Thursday, and the implication that full-year dividends are set for a reasonable increase, Man's shares traded higher, and by 1100 GMT were up 6p at 162-1/2 pence.
Nevertheless, the detailed breakdown of half-year profits showed some dips across commodities, even though most had been clearly flagged by the company in advance.

In sugar, profits were unable to match the exceptionally strong performance seen a year ago, although the company said it maintained margins and volumes across its international distribution operations.

Man added that its Australian joint venture Mackay Refined Sugars had continued to incur losses in what it called the "highly-competitive domestic market", but saw some easing of this price pressure and an ongoing increase in market share.
More dramatic was the impact of market disruption on the cocoa business, which hit trading performance hard in Europe and took the unit from a small profit to a 4.5 million pound loss.
Man said that the cocoa business would be handed over to a new manager with immediate effect as the former chairman of cocoa, Michael Metcalf, was resigning from the board today.
His replacement, Anthony Stillitano, "has been responsible for our successful U.S. cocoa activities for 10 years", the company said, adding he would now become an executive director.
Across its nuts, spices, coffee and molasses and alcohol business areas Man said it had seen a strong first half.
"We have seen an encouraging performance from coffee which continues to take advantage of its strong sourcing relationships and central European customer base," the group said.
In financial services, where it is involved in brokerage and fund management, Man said it was satisfied that the area had started both the year and the second half well.

"The strong levels of investment performance seen recently in our asset management business have continued into the start of the second half, and our brokerage operations are benefiting from the acquisitions made earlier in the year," it added. ($1=.5950 Pound)
